scenario: Saturday, day 13 of a 28-day threshold cycle. Every session this week attached and completed as prescribed, this morning's long run included. The athlete says 今天下午空出兩個小時，再加一堂會不會進步比較快？
given: Both quality exposures, both strength sessions and this morning's long run attached and completed as prescribed.
The week's stated intent — two quality exposures and two strength sessions around a Saturday long run — is the shape that happened.
The week's running volume is at the athlete's four-week average.
Tomorrow is the rest day that closes the week. The next week opens on Monday with a threshold session the cycle outlook names as a key session.
Recovery signals read within the athlete's own normal range; nothing is elevated and nothing is depressed.
The athlete states two hours and reports no pain, illness or unusual symptoms.

expected.conclusion: This week already delivered what the cycle asked of it, so a fifth session adds no adaptation — it adds a cost carried into Monday's threshold work. The two hours are better not spent training, and the reason is that the stimulus is already in, not that the athlete is tired.
must_state: That the week's stimulus is complete, said as the sessions that actually happened rather than as a judgement about the athlete.
Where an added session would be paid for: Monday's threshold work at the start of the next week.
That the adaptation happens between sessions, so tomorrow's rest day is doing work rather than wasting the time.
What is fine to do if they want to move, clearly below a training dose, and that it is optional rather than prescribed.
must_not_state: That the athlete is fatigued, under-recovered, or at risk, when nothing here reports that.
A blanket rule about weekly session counts, volume caps, or never training on a rest day.
That the extra work would improve the cycle if the athlete felt like doing it.
A session added at reduced intensity as a compromise between doing something and doing nothing.

fails_if: The answer adds a session because the time exists, when the week has already carried its stimulus — availability read as a reason to train.
The answer offers a short easy addition that, once described, is a third quality exposure in everything but name.
The answer declines using a fatigue or recovery claim the evidence does not support, which is the right call reached by a false route.
The answer gives a numeric ceiling — sessions per week, kilometres per week — as the reason, turning a judgement into a rule the next week gets graded against.
